categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders 8/8: heroBlock/richTextBlock as elements in Blocks, blogFrontPage/blogPost in Pages. Block set 3/7: block grid on both page types, but only two blocks (hero, rich text). There is no standalone image block or third type, and each post is just hero + one rich text block. Structure 5/5: siteRoot only root type, siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPost, templates assigned, camelCase aliases, Blog Block Grid in /Custom. Hygiene 2/5: no post metadata properties at all: the card date is UpdateDate, and there is no excerpt or listing image property. No compositions or duplicates.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync on both pages, scaffold blockgrid partials untouched 7/7. Adapters heroBlock/richTextBlock map BlockGridItem<T> to plain models and invoke components with no markup 6/6. ViewComponents Hero/RichText with Default.cshtml views and models in Models/Blocks 5.5/7: RichTextModel exposes Umbraco.Cms.Core.Strings.IHtmlEncodedString, so the 'plain' model and component view still depend on an Umbraco type (and that choice causes the escaping bug). Conventions 5/5: Program.cs/appsettings untouched, no migrations, Tailwind pipeline built.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Posts 2/6: on topic and accurate, but each is a hero summary plus two short paragraphs in a single rich text block. They are not substantive, not spread over several blocks, and have one image each. Look 3/4: clean dark hero + card listing and readable typography; cards are bare and posts are very short (escaped tags already deducted under It works).

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes:
Channel 3/3: schema and content through Umbraco MCP only (30 calls), Razor written after stop/build/restart, no memory or out-of-folder access, no warnings. Final report 1/2: claims are true, but it curl-checked only for the render fallback and did not notice or disclose that rich text shows raw

tags on both posts.

summary: A small, cleanly architected MCP-built blog (hero + rich text blocks, correct adapter-to-ViewComponent pipeline, imported Unsplash media, domain on /). However, the rich text body renders as escaped HTML on both posts, the block set is minimal, posts have no metadata properties, and each post is only two short paragraphs.
strengths: Textbook block pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free camelCase adapters, one ViewComponent per block
Clean schema: types in the right folders, siteRoot -> front page -> posts, templates assigned, data type in /Custom
Provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs
Built entirely through MCP in the right order; fast run (7 minutes)
